items.title: Add Hermes Agent integration page
items.body:
Adds a **Hermes Agent** page under Developer Guide ▸ Integrations, after SLNG, for the official Fish Audio plugin for [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent). Electric Sheep maintains the plugin: [100yenadmin/fish-audio-hermes](https://github.com/100yenadmin/fish-audio-hermes), v0.3.0.

The page follows the n8n and SLNG pages:
- prerequisites;
- installation;
- configuration (`hermes fish login`, the desktop app, `hermes fish doctor`);
- choosing a voice (`/fish voices`, `/fish use`, the desktop app's Voices page, and a `config.yaml` example using the Sarah voice);
- features;
- billing notes;
- resources.

**How it was checked**
- Every command on the page ran against Hermes Agent 0.21.5 with the published v0.2.0 release, in a fresh Hermes profile with a real API key. The desktop Voices page (added in v0.3.0) was checked on a development build of Hermes Desktop against the same release. That covers install from GitHub, `hermes fish login`, `hermes fish doctor`, `/fish voices` and voice selection with `hermes fish use`.
- `prettier --check` passes on the new page. In `docs.json`, the only change is one navigation line.
- I couldn't run `mint broken-links` locally: the Mintlify CLI fails on this machine's Node version with a native `sharp` module error. The page has no internal links or custom components.

**Notes for review**
- The page uses the Font Awesome `terminal` icon. Swap it for a Hermes logo if you'd like to add one to `/images`.
- The install line uses the Git URL. Once the plugin's Hermes catalog entry merges (NousResearch/hermes-agent#133221), it can become `hermes plugins install fish-audio --enable`. We'll send that follow-up.
- No audio transcript is included. Your speak-mintlify workflow can generate one if you want it on this page.

items.title: fix(state): read-only SQLite opens find the real database when the path holds #, ? or %

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
Read-only SQLite opens now reach the real database even when its path (usually `HERMES_HOME`) contains `#`, `?` or `%`. Before this change, the gateway readiness probe, the idle-exit kanban check, the hosted-rooms legacy import, `hermes approvals suggest` and the usage-metrics snapshot opened a different file and created an empty database next to the home.

## Before / after (real runs, unmodified `origin/main` vs this branch)

`HERMES_HOME=…/sq/pro#file%41home`. A real `SessionDB` creates `state.db` there with one session, and then the shipped readers run against it:

| reader | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `approvals_suggest._connect_readonly` → `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions` | `OperationalError: no such table: sessions` | `1` |
| shared-metrics `_first_session_started_at` | `OperationalError: no such table: sessions` | `1793000101.93…` |
| gateway readiness `_probe_state_db` | `{'status': 'ok'}`, but read from an empty stray DB, so a corrupt state.db would also read "ok" | `{'status': 'ok'}` from the real state.db |
| files beside the home afterwards | `pro` (stray empty DB) + `pro#file%41home` | `pro#file%41home` only |

## Root cause
`sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)` hands SQLite an unescaped URI. `#` starts the fragment and `?` starts the query, so the path is cut short there. `%xx` is percent-decoded. `mode=ro` sits after the cut, so it is dropped too. SQLite then opens the truncated path read-write-create and leaves an empty database behind. Sites: `gateway/readiness.py`, `gateway/run_idle_exit.py`, `gateway/hosted_rooms_legacy_import.py`, `hermes_cli/approvals_suggest.py`, `hermes_cli/observability/shared_metrics_snapshot.py`, plus two eval scripts and the fastmcp skill template.

## Changes
Every remaining raw site goes through the existing `hermes_state_holders.read_only_db_uri()` (`Path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro"`), which backup, doctor and the session store already use. The eval scripts and the optional fastmcp template do not import Hermes, so they inline the same `as_uri()` form. `hermes_cli/worktree_ops.py` already uses `quote()`, so it is unchanged. Test-only helpers that open fixed temp paths are untouched.

Found while auditing a third-party plugin's workarounds. The earlier attempts #114279 (gateway legacy import) and #122692 (backup) were closed unmerged; backup has since been fixed on `main` (#124066).

## Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_read_only_db_uri_paths.py` (new): homes named `he#rmes`, `he%41rmes` and (POSIX) `he?rmes`. It covers the readiness probe, kanban due-work detection, the hosted-rooms legacy import, and the approvals and metrics readers. Each case also asserts that no stray file appears beside the home. Red on `main`.
- Also run: `tests/gateway/test_hosted_rooms.py`, `tests/gateway/test_unmanaged_idle_exit.py`.

## NOT_COVERED
- A `%` in `HERMES_HOME` also crashes every `hermes` CLI invocation, before any DB open: `ValueError: badly formed help string`. The top-level argparse help embeds the config path (`hermes_cli/_parser.py` `_add_top_level_flags`), and argparse %-formats help strings. That is a separate bug, not fixed here; the live run above therefore calls the readers directly instead of `hermes approvals suggest`.
- Windows: `?` cannot appear in a filename there, so that parameter is POSIX-only.

## Infographic
![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe698/ShLTFPeS8azQHznDG8o5q_bb71j4Fp.png)

items.title: Desktop and TUI: a denied or timed-out command reads Blocked, not Ran
items.body:
When an approval is denied or times out (or a guard refuses the command), the Desktop tool row now reads **Blocked rm -rf …** with "You denied this command — it did not run." under it, instead of **Ran rm -rf …**; the Ink TUI trail says why and marks the call ✗ instead of ✓.

Found while auditing a third-party plugin's workarounds; reproduced live on `main` in the Desktop app.

## What changes

| Surface | Input | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop tool row | approval left to time out (20 s) | `Ran rm -rf …/victim` (red), detail is the model-facing `BLOCKED: … Do NOT retry …` text | `Blocked rm -rf …/victim`, detail `No answer within 20 seconds — the command did not run.` |
| Desktop tool row | Reject clicked | `Ran rm -rf …/victim` (red) | `Blocked rm -rf …/victim`, detail `You denied this command — it did not run.` |
| Desktop run summary | one refused command | `Ran 1 command, 1 tool call failed` | `Blocked rm -rf /srv/data` |
| Desktop run summary | one command that ran + one refused | `Ran 2 commands, 1 tool call failed` | `Ran 1 command, blocked rm -rf /srv/data` |
| Ink TUI trail | approval timed out | `Terminal("rm -rf /srv/data") (0.1s) ✓` | `Terminal("rm -rf /srv/data") (0.1s) :: No answer within 20 seconds — the command did not run. ✗` |
| Classic CLI | any refusal | already honest (`agent/display.py` shows `[You denied this command — it did not run.]` after the row) | unchanged |

Desktop rows are from the live runs below; the summary and TUI rows are from the new tests, which drive the real formatters with the envelope the terminal tool returns.

**Root cause:** the refusal is in the result body (terminal: `status: "blocked"`; execute_code: an error opening with `BLOCKED`; a human decision also adds `user_summary` from `tools/approval.py::_denied`). The Desktop title formatter (`fallback-model/index.ts::dynamicTitle`) and run summary picked the verb from the tool name alone, and the TUI trail always printed ✓, so neither ever looked at that body.

## Changes
- `toolCallBlocked` (Desktop `fallback-model/format.ts`) detects a refusal the same way `agent/context_compressor.py` already does (`status == "blocked"` or a `BLOCKED` error), plus `user_summary`.
- terminal/execute_code rows lead with **Blocked** (new `assistant.tool.actions.blocked` in every Desktop locale; `_keys.desktop.json` regenerated). The row detail leads with `user_summary`, the sentence the CLI already shows, rather than the "Do NOT retry" text written for the model.
- Run summary: a refused command gets its own "Blocked …" clause and is no longer counted under "Ran" or "N tool calls failed". Rows stay red, and they still surface when tool activity is hidden (non-zero `exit_code`).
- TUI: `turnController.recordToolComplete` now takes the `tool.complete` payload, reads the result for a refusal (`lib/toolRefusal.ts`), shows its note and marks the line ✗. This also moves six positional args out of the event handler, which keeps its size ratchet flat.

## Live evidence (native Electron under Xvnc, real `hermes serve` + gateway, scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME/lock dir, loopback stub model asking for `rm -rf <victim>`, `approvals.timeout: 20`)
Turn 1 leaves the approval card to time out. Turn 2 clicks Reject. `victim/keep.txt` survived both runs on both arms, so the command never ran.

**main**: both rows read `Ran rm -rf …` in red

![main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cfbeddfcfa96e0cce007898561092c1/raw/desktop_main_blocked_rows.png)

**this PR**: both rows read `Blocked rm -rf …`, each with its human sentence

![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cfbeddfcfa96e0cce007898561092c1/raw/desktop_head_blocked_rows.png)

## Tests
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/blocked-tool-row.test.ts`: row title/detail for a timed-out terminal call, a hardline block and a denied execute_code, plus the run summary. Red on `main` (`Received: "Ran rm -rf /srv/data"`, `"Ran 1 command, 1 tool call failed"`), green here.
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/toolRefusalTrail.test.ts`: real `createGatewayEventHandler` → trail line. Red on `main` (`'Terminal("rm -rf /srv/data") (0.1s) ✓'`), green here, and a command that ran keeps its ✓.
- Passing: Desktop `tool/` + `thread/` vitest, `npm run check:lint` (0 errors), TUI `typecheck`, `createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts`, `scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking).

## NOT_COVERED
- TUI live PTY A/B: covered by the event-handler test with the real envelope, not by a tmux capture.
- The head screenshot was taken before `shellAction` was pulled out of `dynamicTitle` for the CC ratchet. That move is a pure refactor with the same output, and the tests cover it.

## Infographic

![blocked-not-run](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe803/9kn9Z9tYfHsYcjj8H6ISw_M067vn0k.png)

items.title: feat(tui): rewind to an earlier prompt (/rewind, Esc Esc) and a 'No, tell Hermes instead' approval option (salvage #25074)
items.body:
The Ink TUI can now rewind to any earlier prompt (`/rewind`, or `Esc Esc` on an idle, empty composer), edit it and resend it. Approval prompts gain **"No, and tell Hermes what to do instead"**: the typed instruction is steered into the held turn and the command is denied, so the model gets the denial and your correction together.

Salvage of #25074 (by @SaguaroDev, credited as co-author). See **Salvage** below for what was carried over and what was not.

## Before / after (real `hermes --tui` in tmux, real model)

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `Esc Esc` on an empty composer after 3 turns | nothing happens | rewind picker opens: `▸ 3. …GAMMA` / `2. …BETA` / `1. …ALPHA` |
| `/rewind` | `/rewind is not available on the shared gateway yet` | same picker |
| Pick prompt 1, change it to DELTA, Enter | (base: the DELTA text was sent as a 4th turn; all 8 rows stay active) | `rewound to prompt 1 (6 messages removed)`, the transcript repaints to just DELTA. `state.db`: rows 1–6 `active=0`, rows 7–8 (DELTA) `active=1` |
| Approval for `rm -rf probe_dir` | 4 rows: Allow once / session / always / Deny | 5th row: `No, and tell Hermes what to do instead` |
| Press `5`, type "Do not delete it. Instead list its contents with ls.", Enter | `5` is not a choice and the typed text goes nowhere, so the Enter confirms the highlighted **Allow once** and `probe_dir` is deleted | `steer queued — arrives after next tool call`. The tool result is `BLOCKED: Command denied by user`, followed by the steer and then `Terminal("ls -la probe_dir")`. The reply was "I didn't delete probe_dir. Its contents are a single empty file, keep.txt." `probe_dir/keep.txt` still exists |

Screenshots (base vs head; final head `9126529c0b5` was re-run on both scenarios with the same outcome):

| stage | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Esc Esc after 3 turns | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_rewind_03_esc_esc.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_rewind_03_esc_esc.png) |
| /rewind | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_rewind_08_slash_rewind.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_rewind_05_editing.png) |
| after sending the edit | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_rewind_07_after_send.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_rewind_07_after_send.png) |
| approval prompt | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_approval_01_approval.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_approval_01_approval.png) |
| tell-instead typed / outcome | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_approval_04_after_tell.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_approval_03_tell_typed.png) |
| outcome | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/base_approval_04_after_tell.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/b6173e1a932333c5713365955726a9a0/raw/head_approval_04_after_tell.png) |

The screenshots are plain-text renders of `tmux capture-pane`. The capture `.txt` files and the `state.db` row dumps sit beside them in the run directory.


## What changed

- **Rewind picker** (`ui-tui/src/app/slash/canonicalRewindPicker.ts`, `components/rewindPicker.tsx`). The picker lists the stored user turns newest first, using the same filter `/undo` and `/retry` use (compaction carriers and archived rows are skipped). Enter opens the picked prompt for editing. Enter again sends a revision-fenced `session.mutate rewind {target_message_id: <picked row>}`, repaints the transcript from the owner's snapshot, then sends the edit as an ordinary prompt. **Nothing is cut until the edit is sent.** Esc steps back (edit → list → closed), and Ctrl+C closes the picker. A turn that carried media keeps its number but is not offered, because it has no lossless replay (the `/retry` rule).
- **Esc Esc** opens the picker only on an idle, empty composer with no overlay up. With a draft it still discards the draft. Mid-turn it still interrupts. The Esc that closes an overlay can't count as the first half of the double press. `resolveDoubleEscAction` and its tests are unchanged; the new gate is `shouldOpenRewindOnDoubleEsc`.
- **Tell-instead approval row** (`components/prompts.tsx`, `app/useApprovalAnswers.ts`, `app/steerOrQueue.ts`). The row appears wherever the gateway offers Deny. `approvalOptions` still returns exactly the gateway's choices, and the row is added by `approvalRows`. Picking the row keeps the command held while you type. On Enter the TUI calls `session.steer` **first**, so the instruction rides on the blocked tool result, and then sends the gateway a plain `deny`. If the steer is refused because the turn already ended, the words are queued as the next prompt, the same fallback `/steer` uses. Esc on the typing row returns to the choices; Esc on the choices still denies outright.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/tui.md` (keybindings and the `/rewind` row in the slash table). New hotkey row. i18n keys go in their topical en siblings, and `locales/_keys.tui.json` was regenerated.
- Code-health: the approval answers moved from `useMainApp` into the `useApprovalAnswers` sibling hook, and the double-Esc branch moved from the `useInputHandlers` key handler into `runDoubleEsc`. Both functions end up under their main values.

## Why it's safe for the prompt cache

Rewind is user-initiated history truncation, the same class as `/undo`. It uses the existing owner primitive (`hermes_state_rewind.py` soft-delete via `session.mutate rewind`), not a new path. The steer goes through the existing `session.steer` (the current-turn tool-result slot), so the system prompt and toolsets are never touched.

## Salvage

- **#25074** (open, @SaguaroDev) and its predecessor **#23445** (closed unmerged). Issue #21910 was closed as completed, but neither PR merged, and `origin/main` has no picker anywhere: Ink has only last-turn `/undo` and `/retry`. Those PRs added their own `messages.active` column, a schema-v13 bump, a CLI `/rewind`, and gateway thread-scoped deletion of platform messages. Main has since landed its own soft-delete rewind (`hermes_state_rewind.py`, `session.mutate rewind`, used by `/undo` and `/retry` and by Desktop's edit-and-resend). The schema, DB and CLI commits therefore don't apply to the current facade layout, and they would duplicate that primitive. What is carried over is the UX those PRs designed: pick a prior prompt, prefill it, re-prompt. @SaguaroDev is co-author on the feature commit.
- Not carried over, and still open in #25074: rewind from messaging platforms (gateway thread scope plus best-effort deletion of Discord/Telegram messages), and a classic-CLI `/rewind`.

Refs #25693: the TUI half. The classic CLI and messaging-platform approval surfaces are NOT_COVERED below, so the issue stays open.

## Tests

- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/canonicalRewindPicker.test.ts` (new) checks the picker's targets and numbering, that nothing is mutated before send, that the rewind targets the PICKED row with the snapshot CAS, the busy refusal at send time, that the picker doesn't open mid-turn, and the idle double-Esc gate matrix.
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/approvalTell.test.ts` (new) checks where the row appears, number-key selection, that Esc still denies, steer-and-no-queue on success, and queue-on-refusal or failure.
- Both files import symbols that don't exist on base, so they are red on `origin/main`. The full ui-tui vitest suite passes (`npx vitest run`, exit 0), and so do `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, `npm run i18n:keys:check`, `python scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking) and `git diff --check`. Every `origin/main` approval, input-handler and canonical-slash test passes unchanged.

## Live verification

Rung 4: a real `hermes --tui` in a tmux PTY. Each arm used a fake `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME` and its own isolated gateway lock dir. The model was `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` on Nous inference. The Python tree is the same for both arms (this PR changes no Python). Only the TUI bundle differs (`HERMES_TUI_DIR` pointing at a `scripts/build/tui.mjs` build of base or head). Billed: about $0.012 total ($0.0036 + $0.0024 base; $0.0027 + $0.0010 + $0.0010 + $0.0006 head, including the re-run on the final head).

## NOT_COVERED

- **Classic CLI** tell-instead row and `/rewind`. `hermes_cli/cli_tui_mixin.py` is 2,313 lines (over the 2,000 cap), and its Enter routing would need a typing sub-state. That belongs in a follow-up that also splits the file.
- **Desktop**: it has its own approval component (not shared with Ink), so the tell-instead row there is a follow-up. Desktop already has edit-and-resend for rewind.
- The **legacy (non-shared) gateway** transport: `/rewind` prints that it needs the shared gateway. Ink's default path is the shared gateway.
- **Messaging-platform rewind** (#25074's gateway half).

## Design choices a maintainer may rule differently

- Idle `Esc Esc` now opens the picker; before, it did nothing. The picker is non-destructive (Esc closes it), so this isn't behind a config flag.
- The cut happens at **send**, not at pick, so the user can back out of a pick without losing history.
- Tell-instead **steers first, then denies**, rather than denying first. Denying first would let the model act on the bare denial before the instruction arrives.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe68b/nSrtlu2Ioxt6wY7LFzofo_Tyvj4cBv.png)

items.title: chore(sync): merge upstream v0.22.5
items.body:
## Summary

Resolves weekly upstream sync. Merges `NousResearch/hermes-agent` tag `v0.22.5` into `main` as a real two-parent merge commit.

**Target tag:** `v0.22.5` — selected via `scripts/ci/pick_upstream_tag.py` on `origin/main` (highest semver tag merged in `upstream/main`).

Closes #189

## Hand-resolved files

| File | Resolution |
|------|-----------|
| `.github/workflows/desktop-bundle-smoke.yml` | Both sides moved Windows runners away from Blacksmith (Playwright fails there). Fork used `windows-11-arm`/`windows-2025`; upstream used `windows-latest-32-arm-core`/`windows-latest-32-core` with an explanatory comment. Took upstream's specific runner names and comment; both sides had the same intent. |
| `README.md` | Fork added the "Alternate Runtimes" section (Letta brain mode docs). Upstream renamed "Migrating from OpenClaw" → "Migrating from OpenClaw or another agent". Kept both: the fork's section is preserved, the heading uses upstream's updated text. |
| `uv.lock` | Fork added `pymupdf` to the hermes-agent dependency listing; upstream refactored `pyopen-wakeword` marker expressions (logical equivalence, different syntax). Kept `pymupdf` from fork + upstream's marker syntax. `uv` was not available on this host to regenerate the lockfile; CI will validate. |

## Tests run

- `python3 -m compileall -q` over `agent/`, `gateway/`, `tools/`, `hermes_cli/`, `plugins/`, `acp_adapter/`, `tests/` — **clean** (no errors)
- `pytest` was not available in the host environment; full test suite runs on CI

## Merge instructions

Merge with "Create a merge commit". Squash or rebase destroys the upstream parent.
